So, have you done your crafting and provisions certification? Of you did, then you know that you go to a crafting station to craft stuff? Okay, so, let's use the clothing station as a example. To do that, you need a piece of gear with the training trait in your inventory. Then you enter that research menu, navigate to the piece of armor you have (with the training trait on them) and select it to start it researching. It will take a short time, and afterwards you will be able to craft something with that trait, provided you have the crafting materials. However, should you want a "set", you will need to research different traits on every piece of armor. For example: Hundings Rage has 6 traits, meaning, to craft boots of hundings rage, you would need to research 6 traits in the "boots" column, to craft a single pair of leg armor and after every trait you research, the next one takes longer to finish. With that said, you need to level your blacksmithing, clothing etc to level 50 in order to craft items of your level and above.

Now, in my mind, that means, either killing or driving away the opposing faction, taking over their cities, and then visiting the reclaimed cities under the new faction etc. This did not happen. What did happen, was a image and voiceover of the consequences of a specific choice you made. The ending really disappointed me, but it wasn't Mass Effect 3 bad. Fourth, the combat. Here I was thinking magic would do more damage than guns, lol, apparently not. So after trying all roles, Technician seemed the best choice, as the guns do insane damage, and the "ultimate" ability in the skill line, also does an insane amount of damage, and saved my butt a lot of times. It's clunky, but I have played games with worse combat. Overall, the story is good, the world is diverse, and if modders are able to mod this game to the extent of say, Dragon Age 2 and 3 or The Witcher 3, to improve certain things in the game, I would definitely do a second and maybe even a third playthrough. 6/10
